title: How Ravi Kishan Became India's Biggest Meme Sensation and Gen Z's Unlikely Icon
excerpt: The 57-year-old actor-politician's verbal goof-ups, Bhojpuri film clips, and unfiltered charm have made him the internet's most beloved personality — a phenomenon now reaching European football clubs.
body:
• Actor-politician Ravi Kishan has become India's biggest meme sensation, with viral clips ranging from verbal goof-ups like "home from work" and "jaldi the late" to spirited dance moves and devotional singing
  • European football clubs Juventus and Borussia Dortmund have recreated his viral moments on Instagram, pushing his meme fame beyond Indian borders
  • The 57-year-old BJP MP from Gorakhpur says his viral moments are never planned, crediting icons from "Al Pacino to Michael Jackson" for his flamboyant style

Somewhere between Parliament sessions and film promotions, Ravi Kishan became the internet's favorite person. The 57-year-old Bhojpuri cinema veteran and BJP MP from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh has spent the past several weeks at the center of an ever-expanding meme universe — one built not on mockery but genuine affection, and one that has now crossed national borders.

The Viral Moments That Started It All

The current wave began earlier this year when a clip of Kishan outside Parliament went viral. Surrounded by reporters, he accidentally said "jaldi the late" — a Hindi-English mashup that made no grammatical sense in either language but perfectly captured his unfiltered charm. Months later, another clip surfaced of him saying "home from work" instead of "work from home," triggering a fresh meme cycle.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2087126270148817057

Then came the "Headquarters" moment. On Amazon Prime Video's reality show Alliance, Kishan departed early to attend to his constituency duties. While explaining his exit to fellow contestants, he said he had been summoned for national duty and needed to leave the "headquarters" immediately — a line that quickly became internet shorthand, according to Bollywood Hungama.

From Bhojpuri Clips to European Football

In mid-July, a clip from the 2012 Bhojpuri film Kanoon Hamra Mutthi Mein broke the internet. The scene features Kishan's character struggling in a tag-team arm-wrestling match before receiving a kiss from co-star Nagma, which gives him a surge of energy — complete with lightning effects — to overpower his opponents. Then a months-old video of him passionately singing the devotional song "Har Har Bhole Namah Shivaya" went viral, opening the floodgates to what Bollywood Hungama described as "a Ravi Kishan special week on the internet."

Netizens began unearthing clip after clip — Kishan and fellow MP Manoj Tiwari hilariously arguing in English, Kishan dancing with abandon at promotional events, Kishan declaring his "maun vrat" (vow of silence) outside Parliament to dodge reporters' questions. The meme phenomenon reached Europe when football giants Juventus and Borussia Dortmund recreated his viral moments on their Instagram accounts, with Juventus compiling his greatest hits.

"I'm from Al Pacino to Amitabh Bachchan to Balraj Sahni to Shah Rukh Khan to Michael Jackson to Elvis Presley… Itni saare log mere sharir mein naachte, gaate rehte hain."

— Ravi Kishan, speaking to News18

Why Gen Z Loves Him

What separates Kishan from celebrities who awkwardly chase internet relevance is his complete lack of self-consciousness. Speaking to News18 about his meme fame, he said: "I'm not trying anything. I'm not reading anything. It's just the moment I come, and something happens to my body, and words nikalte hai."

At the trailer launch of the Netflix film Maa Behen, he addressed his viral status with characteristic humor: "I swear on Mahadev, mujhe nahi malum main kyun viral hota hoon! People look at me as if I've come from some different planet. I'm human, and I make mistakes just like all of you," he said, according to Filmfare.

Social media captions like "Protect him, he's a national treasure" and "National crush" have become standard on his viral clips. At the Mirzapur: The Movie trailer launch on August 11, co-stars recreated his famous one-liners in tribute, reported Bollywood Hungama. Even at the Dhamaal 4 launch, he turned his 2013 Bhojpuri film Dhurandhar — which benefited from the buzz around the 2025 Bollywood film of the same name — into a punchline, joking that its producers "have suddenly become crorepatis now."

A Career Built for This Moment

Kishan's career has been a slow build across languages and industries. After early Hindi films, Tere Naam (2003) brought him attention. His turn as the lisping sidekick in Phir Hera Pheri (2006) and his appearance on Bigg Boss Season 1 made him a household name. More recently, Laapataa Ladies (2024) and the Netflix series Maamla Legal Hai reinforced his range. His latest, Dhamaal 4 with Ajay Devgn, has crossed Rs 158 crore at the domestic box office.

But it is the internet's embrace of his unscripted, off-camera self that has defined 2026 for Ravi Kishan. As Bollywood Hungama put it: "At a time when the older generation is struggling to connect with Gen Z, Ravi Kishan offers a simple lesson in how it can be done: be yourself."
nri_angle: Ravi Kishan's meme phenomenon resonates with diaspora audiences who grew up with Bhojpuri and Hindi cinema and are watching Gen Z in India reclaim these cultural icons through internet humor.
author: Diaspora Desk
